From Old East Slavic годъ (godŭ, “time, period, year, age”), from Proto-Slavic *godъ (“suitable time”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *gadás, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰodʰo-, from *gʰedʰ- (“to unite, be associated, be suitable”). Cognates include Ukrainian годі (hodi, “enough”), Bulgarian годе (gode, “ever”) (as in кой-годе (koj-gode) = whoever), Czech hod, Polish gody (“yearly feast”), Upper Sorbian hody (“Christmas”), Lower Sorbian gódy (“Christmas”), Latvian gadigs. Germanic cognates include German Gatte (“husband”), gätlich (“convenient”), Dutch gegade, gade, gading, Dutch gader, goed, German…
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic достоиновѣрьнъ (dostoinověrĭnŭ), a calque of Ancient Greek ἀξιόπιστος (axiópistos). By surface analysis, досто- (dosto-) + ве́рный (vérnyj).
